counterfactual_missing_items: No culture or PCR-based identification of Mucorales is reported.
Only a presumptive diagnosis of deep cutaneous fungal infection was made at this time.
No clinical response to itraconazole or surgical debridement is documented.
decisive_items: tender, warm, erythematous nodular skin lesions appeared on the lower limbs and then the upper limbs; the lesions progressed to central ulceration with a necrotic core.
thin-walled (5–15 μm), pauciseptate hyphae with minimal branching
thick-walled ovoid sporangia (5–20 μm) that stained strongly with PAS, GMS, and Giemsa
response.rationale: C1 combines the same angioinvasive, pauciseptate, sporangia-forming fungal morphology captured by R3 with the additional, separately supported cutaneous localization (limb nodules progressing to necrosis, left-thigh punch biopsy). R3 is a correct near-identical diagnosis but lacks the anatomic modifier; this is an append-only completion, so the margin is low. R1 is contradicted by fungal microbial structures and sporangia rather than lymphoma histology; R2 reflects a predisposing complication, not the tissue diagnosis.

rejected.why: CLL and nodular lesions are nonspecific; histopathology shows angioinvasive fungal structures and sporangia, not a clonal lymphocytic infiltrate, so cutaneous lymphoma is unsupported.
Neutropenia and fever are risk factors/complications in the timeline, but the diagnosis is provided by biopsy findings of invasive fungal elements, not by sepsis as a pathologic entity.
